summary.one_liner: A curated, alphabetically sorted awesome-list of developer environment tools, dotfile collections, editor plugins and workflow utilities, grouped by category.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" link list rather than a tool. It is organized into categories such as Admins, Benchmarking, Data, Diagnostics, Desktop, Documentation, Dotfiles, Editors (Atom, Vim, Sublime Text, IntelliJ, VS Code), Git, Shell, Terminal, Text, Presentation, Orchestration and Workflow. Each entry is a one-line description of a tool, with OS tags like /OSX/ or /WIN/ where relevant. Examples include load-testing tools (ab, wrk, vegeta, siege), git helpers (hub, git-extras, tig), shell frameworks (oh-my-zsh, fish, zgen), and search tools (ripgrep, ag, ack). The README describes its contribution rules: entries are alphabetically sorted and inappropriate items are handled via issues.
use_cases: find a command-line tool for a specific developer task
discover shell frameworks and zsh plugins
pick editor plugins for Vim, Atom, Sublime or VS Code
notable: Organized by category with short descriptions and OS tags (OSX/WIN/*NIX/LIN)
Includes curated dotfile repository links such as thoughtbot and Mathias Bynens
Covers editor plugins for Atom, Vim, Sublime Text, IntelliJ and VS Code
Inspired by awesome-go and awesome-python and follows their contribution style
caveats: Links are not verified and many entries are one-line descriptions only, so some tools may be outdated
Several entries are OS-specific (mostly OSX), limiting use on other platforms
No install instructions because it is a list, not software
